title: Resonant enhancement of Raman scattering in a MoS$_2$ nanotube
authors: D. R. Kazanov, A. V. Poshakinskiy
abstract: The whispering-gallery modes confined in the wall of a multiwall MoS$_2$ nanotube resonantly enhance the spontaneous Raman scattering by its own optical phonons. The enhancement is doubly resonant --- pump and Stokes waves hit two adjacent modes at one pump energy, and the signal scales as $(Q_{\rm pump}Q_{\rm sc})^2$ - whenever a phonon energy matches the free spectral range of the mode ladder. Near the A exciton the excitonic dispersion compresses the ladder and sweeps its spacing through all intralayer phonon energies of MoS$_2$, so the match, reached for $A_{1g}$ at $E_{\rm pump}=1551$~meV, requires no geometric tuning. A missed match splits the excitation peak into a pump- and a scattered-resonant doublet whose splitting measures the residual detuning. Selection rules confine the double resonance to the TM$\to$TM channel and exclude $E_{1g}$.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that the confined optical modes (WGMs) within a MoS2 nanotube can act as a highly efficient resonator for spontaneous Raman scattering. By exploiting the exciton-induced compression of the WGM spectrum, the system achieves a double resonance matching the phonon energy, leading to massive signal enhancement.
main_problem: The paper investigates the resonant enhancement of spontaneous Raman scattering in a MoS2 nanotube, driven by the nanotube's own optical phonons.
main_result: The system exhibits a double resonance in the TM->TM scattering channel, achieving an enhancement exceeding the non-resonant level by four orders of magnitude without requiring geometric fine-tuning.
method: The analysis uses electromagnetic calculations to model Whispering-Gallery Modes (WGMs) and calculates the Raman intensity using the incoherent sum formula, incorporating resonance matching factors.
model_or_system: The physical system is a multiwall MoS2 nanotube, modeled as a hollow shell supporting TM-polarized WGMs. The core mechanism involves the Free Spectral Range (FSR) of these WGMs sweeping across the intralayer phonon energies near the A exciton.
key_observables: Raman scattering intensity, the matching factor $ho(\delta)$, and the polarization-dependent scattering channels ($	ext{TM}	o	ext{TM}$, $	ext{TM}	o	ext{TE}$, etc.).
important_parameters: Phonon energies ($	ext{A}_{1	ext{g}}$, $	ext{E}_{1	ext{g}}$, $	ext{E}_{2	ext{g}}$), the exciton energy, and the detuning parameter $\delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis separates the problem into TM and TE polarizations, treating the nanotube as a hollow shell, and uses the assumption of double resonance when phonon energy matches the FSR.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup showing the pumping and scattering process, and show the FSR of the WGM pair versus phonon energy, demonstrating the compression and self-tuning effect.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model using WGMs, derives the resonance condition based on the FSR matching the phonon energy, analyzes the intensity using the matching factor $ho(\delta)$, and finally compares the enhancement across different polarization channels.
why_interesting: The concept of using confined photonic modes (WGMs) to engineer strong, tunable resonances for inelastic light scattering is highly relevant to quantum optics and cavity QED, suggesting a pathway for enhancing weak quantum signals.
